epic.title: Customer success manager twin for Example Software Co

stories.title: Account brief before a customer call
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin to account brief before a customer call so that I get the one-page account brief.

fields.connectors_and_identity: hubspot: user identity, read, always-allow; google-drive: user identity, read, always-allow
fields.inputs: hubspot (company, contacts, deals, open tickets, notes); google-drive (account plan, last QBR deck, contract)
fields.output_and_audience: One-page account brief, internal; to none (the conversation)
fields.baseline: 6 per week x 30 minutes each x 8 users

acceptance: Eval from good example 1 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from good example 2 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from bad example 1 of 1 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin does not repeat the mistake.

tasks.title: Collect 3 examples of the task from real work, each with the result a person expects

how.text: Ask the people who do the task today for three recent, real examples of it.
Record each example's inputs and the output a person would accept as done.
Remove any data the examples must not carry into the repository, keeping their shape.

tasks.done_when: Three real examples, each with its inputs and its expected result, are stored where the evals can read them.

tasks.title: Write the evals from the examples and the story's acceptance criteria

how.text: Turn each example and each acceptance criterion into an eval case with its expected result.
Put the eval cases in the files the kit expects, next to the skill.
Run the evals once before any skill exists and keep the failing baseline.

tasks.done_when: Every acceptance criterion has at least one eval, and the evals run and fail without the skill.

tasks.title: Write the skill from the kit template until the evals pass

how.text: Copy the kit's skill template into the role plugin's skills folder.
Rename the copy to the skill's name.
Fill in the description and the body, then rerun the evals until they pass.

tasks.done_when: The skill sits in the role plugin and every eval for the story passes.

tasks.title: Write and run the trigger evals for the skill

how.text: Install skill-creator where the evals run.
Write prompts that should and should not start the skill, as trigger evals.
Run the trigger evals and tighten the description until they pass.

tasks.done_when: The skill starts on every should-trigger prompt and on none of the should-not prompts.

tasks.title: Have a second person review the skill and its evals

how.text: Open a pull request with the skill and its evals.
Have someone other than the author review it against the definition of done.

tasks.done_when: A reviewer who did not write the skill has approved the pull request and the evals pass.

tasks.title: Publish the skill in the role plugin

how.text: Add the skill to the role plugin and bump the plugin's version.
Publish the marketplace so the role's users get the new version.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user in the role sees the skill after the plugin updates.

tasks.title: Connect it without a kit runbook: the kit has no runbook for this connector yet (hubspot)

how.text: Check how the system connects today: a directory connector, a vendor server or none.
If the directory has no connector for it, choose to buy, build or host one.
Review the connector before it is enabled, and write down the steps you followed.

tasks.done_when: The connector works for a pilot user with the planned identity, and the steps are written down for a runbook.

how.text: Open the connector's page in the Claude org and find the tool.
Set the tool to Always allow and record the change.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 2, act with approval

how.text: Show the evals pass reliably at the current level.
Bring a month of scorecard results, with the edit rate, to the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the move to level 2 on scorecard evidence, and the tool settings are changed.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 3, act within an allowlist

how.text: Confirm every allowlisted action can be undone or stays internal.
Show a stable eval pass rate, a low edit rate and few rejections at level 2.
List the tools to set to Always allow and keep every other tool on Needs approval.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the allowlist on scorecard evidence, and only those tools are Always allow.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (connectors.google-drive)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Resolve warning confidential-standard-retention: set custom retention or record the customer's acceptance

how.text: Explain that page 10 requires custom retention for confidential data, otherwise local sessions are kept 6 years.
On Enterprise, set custom retention; on Team, record that the customer accepts standard retention.

tasks.done_when: Custom retention is set, or the customer's acceptance of standard retention is recorded.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 3, act within an allowlist

how.text: Confirm every allowlisted action can be undone or stays internal.
Show a stable eval pass rate, a low edit rate and few rejections at level 2.
List the tools to set to Always allow and keep every other tool on Needs approval.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the allowlist on scorecard evidence, and only those tools are Always allow.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (runtime)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (plan_fit)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (connectors.zendesk)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Resolve warning memory-poisoning-risk: keep memory writes to controlled steps for the task that reads untrusted input

how.text: Explain how untrusted input can poison memory, and that memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch.
Keep role knowledge in reviewed skills and build the task so it never writes memory; only controlled steps write it.
If the org cannot keep memory writes to controlled steps, ask the Owner to switch memory off org-wide.

tasks.done_when: The evals show the task writes nothing to memory, its role knowledge lives in reviewed skills, and the org's memory setting is agreed.

tasks.title: Resolve warning event-source-unverified: confirm what would start the task on its event

how.text: Ask Anthropic and the vendor what can fire the event.
Let a person start the task until the event source is confirmed, then level again.

tasks.done_when: The event source is confirmed in writing, or the task stays person-started.

tasks.title: Resolve warning connector-early-access: confirm the early-access connector with the vendor

how.text: Ask the vendor about the connector's plan support and per-user checks.
Record the answer with its source before the build.

tasks.done_when: The vendor's answer is recorded with its source.

tasks.title: Resolve warning confidential-standard-retention: set custom retention or record the customer's acceptance

how.text: Explain that page 10 requires custom retention for confidential data, otherwise local sessions are kept 6 years.
On Enterprise, set custom retention; on Team, record that the customer accepts standard retention.

tasks.done_when: Custom retention is set, or the customer's acceptance of standard retention is recorded.

stories.title: Persona voice
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's persona voice in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: persona.md is filled in from the card's voice section, with a reason for every rule.
The output style and the system prompt match persona.md.
The business owner has approved the voice.

tasks.title: Fill in the persona from the kit template, from the card's voice section

how.text: Copy the kit's persona template.
Fill in persona.md section by section from the card's voice, giving the reason for every rule.

tasks.done_when: persona.md is filled in with no FILL IN marker left.

tasks.title: Build the output style and the system prompt from the persona

how.text: Build each form the role's surfaces need from persona.md.
Change persona.md and both forms in the same pull request, never one alone.

tasks.done_when: Both forms match persona.md and sit where each surface reads them.

tasks.title: Have the business owner and a pilot user review the persona voice

how.text: Show the reviewers drafts from the twin with the persona in place.
Record what they change and update persona.md and both forms.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the persona voice.

stories.title: Connectors and identity
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's connectors and identity in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: Every connector the role uses is listed with its identity and approver.
The role's users are in the organisation with the right role.

tasks.title: Resolve warning hubspot-super-admin-approval: book the HubSpot approval

how.text: Name the customer's HubSpot Super Admin, or a user with App Marketplace access, in the profile's owners.
Book the approval alongside the Claude Owner's.

tasks.done_when: A HubSpot Super Admin, or a user with App Marketplace access, has approved the connector.

tasks.title: Invite the role's users and set their roles by hand

how.text: Invite each user of the role to the organisation.
Record who is in the role, since the plan has no group to hold them.

tasks.done_when: Every user of the role is in the organisation with the right role, and the list is recorded.

tasks.title: List every connector the role uses, its identity and who approves it

how.text: List the systems each task reads or writes and the connector for each.
Record each connector's identity and the person who approves it.

tasks.done_when: Every connector the role uses is listed with its identity and approver.

tasks.title: Review each connector before it is enabled

how.text: Review each connector against the kit's review questions.
Record the review and any limits it sets.

tasks.done_when: A security reviewer has checked every connector before it is enabled.

stories.title: Guardrails and settings
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's guardrails and settings in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The settings, or what replaces them, are in force for the role.
Compliance has signed off the data policy for each data class.

tasks.title: Resolve warning team-no-managed-settings: put the guardrails in tool permissions and skills

how.text: List the guardrails that managed settings would have locked.
Move each one into a connector tool permission or a skill, and tell the customer what cannot be locked.

tasks.done_when: Each guardrail is enforced by a tool permission or a skill, or listed as not lockable and accepted.

tasks.title: Resolve warning confidential-on-team: confirm the lower audit need for confidential data on Team

how.text: Explain what Team lacks for confidential data.
Get the compliance owner's written confirmation that the lower audit need holds.

tasks.done_when: The compliance owner has confirmed in writing that confidential data on Team is acceptable.

tasks.title: Record what the twin relies on in place of a managed-settings baseline

how.text: List what a baseline would have enforced.
Record what replaces each item, or that nothing does.

tasks.done_when: The design lists what replaces the baseline and the customer has accepted it.

tasks.title: Agree the data policy for each of the role's data classes with compliance

how.text: Take each data class the role's tasks hold through the decision matrix.
Agree the device policy for each class.

tasks.done_when: Compliance has signed off the data policy for every data class the role holds.

stories.title: Distribution
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's distribution in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The role plugin reaches the role's users at the current version, and no one else it must not reach.

tasks.title: Resolve warning team-no-group-targeting: keep the role plugin safe for everyone in the org

how.text: Explain that on Team the role plugin goes to everyone.
Check the role plugin holds nothing other roles must not see.

tasks.done_when: The role plugin holds nothing another role must not see, or the customer has chosen Enterprise.

tasks.title: Create the role plugin from the kit template

how.text: Copy and rename the role-plugin template.
Add the persona and the skills, and the marketplace entry.

tasks.done_when: The role plugin is in the marketplace and its tests pass.

tasks.title: Publish the role plugin to the whole organisation

how.text: Publish the role plugin for every member.
Tell the other roles the plugin is not meant for them.

tasks.done_when: Every member can install the role plugin and the role's users have it.

stories.title: Governance log
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's governance log in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: What is logged for the twin, and where, is agreed and checked.

tasks.title: Resolve warning team-no-governance-log: record use without the governance hook

how.text: Explain that the governance log is a Claude Code hook a Team twin on the web does not get.
Record use from the usage dashboard and the source systems' own audit instead.

tasks.done_when: The design says what is recorded instead of the governance log, and the customer has accepted it.

tasks.title: Resolve warning team-no-audit-log: rely on the source systems' audit logs

how.text: Explain that Team has no audit log and no Compliance API.
Confirm each source system's own audit covers what compliance needs.

tasks.done_when: Compliance has accepted the source systems' audit in place of Claude's audit log.

tasks.title: Record what is logged for this twin without the governance hook

how.text: List what the plan and surface record without the hook.
Write it into the design and get the customer's acceptance.

tasks.done_when: The design says what is logged for the twin and the customer has accepted it.

tasks.title: Turn on the source systems' own audit for the twin's writes

how.text: Check each system the twin writes keeps an audit of changes.
Turn it on where it is off and record how long it is kept.

tasks.done_when: Every system the twin writes keeps an audit of its changes.

stories.title: Memory policy
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's memory policy in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The memory policy is written down and in force.

tasks.title: Write down the role's memory policy

how.text: Decide what the twin may remember for the role and what it must not.
Write the policy into the design and the persona.

tasks.done_when: The memory policy is written down and the business owner has approved it.

tasks.title: Tell the pilot users what memory keeps and how to clear it

how.text: Explain what personal memory keeps and which tasks keep it off.
Show the pilot users how to see and clear what it keeps.

tasks.done_when: Every pilot user knows what memory keeps and how to clear it.

stories.title: Pilot rollout and scorecard
stories.statement: As a Customer success manager, I want my twin's pilot rollout and scorecard in place so that every task story runs safely.
acceptance: The pilot users are trained, the baseline is recorded, and the first scorecard is reviewed.

tasks.title: Name the pilot users and agree the pilot dates

how.text: Choose five to ten pilot users in the role.
Agree the start and review dates with the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The pilot users and dates are agreed and recorded.

tasks.title: Record the baseline time for each pilot task before the pilot starts

how.text: Take each pilot story's baseline from its fields table.
Confirm it with the pilot users before they start.

tasks.done_when: Every pilot task has a baseline agreed with its users.

tasks.title: Set up the monthly scorecard for the twin

how.text: Choose the adoption, quality, value and safety measures for the scorecard.
Book the monthly review with the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The first monthly scorecard has been reviewed with the business owner.

tasks.title: Train the pilot users and tell them how to report a failure

how.text: Run a short session on what the twin does, at what level, and what it never does.
Give the pilot users one place to report a failure or a wrong draft.

tasks.done_when: Every pilot user has been trained and knows where to report a failure.
